code.title: Echo the Array Elements
code.description:
A data entry clerk wants to confirm what was just typed into the terminal. Read N and then N integers, store them in an array and print them back separated by single spaces on one line.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N array elements.

Output Format:
The N integers separated by single spaces on one line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000 <= element <= 1000

code.title: Index and Value Listing
code.description:
A lab technician labels every sample with its rack slot number. Read N and then N integers into an array, then walk the array and print each index (0-based) together with the value stored there.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N array elements.

Output Format:
For every index i from 0 to N - 1, one line:
Index <i>: <value>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000 <= element <= 1000

code.title: Array Element Sum Drill
code.description:
A cashier totals the day's transactions stored in a list. Read N and then N integers into an array, add them up while traversing the array and print the total.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N array elements.

Output Format:
Sum: <total>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= element <= 10000

code.title: Find the Maximum Element
code.description:
A crane operator wants to know the heaviest load lifted today. Read N and then N integers into an array, then scan the array to find the largest value.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N array elements.

Output Format:
Maximum: <largest value>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= element <= 10000

code.title: Count the Even Numbers
code.description:
A parking lot warden logs vehicle counts per hour and wants to know how many hours had an even number of vehicles. Read N and then N integers into an array, then count how many of them are even.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N array elements.

Output Format:
Even count: <number of even elements>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000 <= element <= 1000

code.title: Elements at Even Indexes
code.description:
A theatre lighting board activates only the fixtures sitting at even slot numbers. Read N and then N integers into an array, then print the elements that sit at indexes 0, 2, 4, ... (0-based even indexes) separated by single spaces on one line.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N array elements.

Output Format:
The elements at even indexes separated by single spaces on one line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000 <= element <= 1000

code.title: Sensor Readings Report
code.description:
A weather station logs N temperature readings for the day. Read N and then N integer readings into an array, then print the total of all readings and the average with exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N readings.

Output Format:
Total: <sum>
Average: <average with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= reading <= 100

code.title: Shopping Cart Subtotal
code.description:
An online store totals the items in a shopper's cart. Read N and then N integer item prices into an array, then print the subtotal by adding every price.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N item prices.

Output Format:
Subtotal: <sum> rupees

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= price <= 5000

code.title: Attendance Register Count
code.description:
A class teacher marks the register as a list of 0s and 1s, one value per student (1 = present, 0 = absent). Read N and then N attendance values into an array, then count how many students are present and how many are absent.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N attendance values (each 0 or 1).

Output Format:
Present: <count of 1s>
Absent: <count of 0s>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, each value is 0 or 1

code.title: Queue Token Min and Max
code.description:
A token dispenser issued N tokens today. Read N and then N token numbers into an array, then report the smallest and the largest token issued.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N token numbers.

Output Format:
Smallest token: <minimum>
Largest token: <maximum>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= token <= 9999

code.title: Roll Number Finder
code.description:
During a surprise audit a teacher searches the roll list for a particular roll number. Read N, then N roll numbers into an array, then the target roll number. Search the array from the start; if the target appears, print the position of its first occurrence using 1-based numbering, otherwise print Not Found.

Input Format:
One line with N + 2 integers: N, the N roll numbers, then the target roll number.

Output Format:
Found at position <1-based position of the first occurrence>
or
Not Found

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= roll number <= 9999

code.title: Defect Occurrence Counter
code.description:
A quality inspector recorded an inspection code for every unit on the belt and now needs the failure count for one specific defect code. Read N, then N codes into an array, then the defect code to look up. Count how many array elements are equal to the defect code.

Input Format:
One line with N + 2 integers: N, the N inspection codes, then the defect code.

Output Format:
Occurrences: <count>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= code <= 100

code.title: Auction Runner-up Bid
code.description:
An auction house recorded N bids. The highest bid wins; the runner-up is the highest bid that is strictly lower than the winning bid. Read N and then N bids into an array, then report both values.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N bids.

Output Format:
Highest bid: <maximum>
Runner-up bid: <second highest distinct value>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= bid <= 100000, at least two distinct bid values exist
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= bid <= 100000, at least two distinct bid values exist

code.title: Train Coach Reversal
code.description:
A yard engine shunts a train so that the last coach becomes the first. Read N and then N coach numbers into an array, reverse the array in place using two indexes and a temporary variable (no STL), then print the reversed array separated by single spaces on one line.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N coach numbers.

Output Format:
The reversed array elements separated by single spaces on one line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= coach number <= 9999

code.title: Conveyor Belt Rotation
code.description:
A packaging line shifts boxes left along the belt by K slots; boxes that fall off the front re-enter at the back. Read N, then N box codes into an array, then K. Rotate the array left by K positions manually (no STL) and print the result separated by single spaces on one line.

Input Format:
One line with N + 2 integers: N, the N box codes, then K.

Output Format:
The rotated array elements separated by single spaces on one line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= K < N, 1 <= box code <= 9999

code.title: Ballot Frequency Report
code.description:
An electronic ballot box logged N votes as candidate IDs between 0 and 100. Read N and then N votes into an array, then produce the tally: print every distinct candidate ID in the order it was first seen, each with the number of votes it received.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N candidate IDs.

Output Format:
For each distinct ID in first-seen order, one line:
Candidate <id>: <votes>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= candidate ID <= 100

code.title: Warehouse Aisle Picker
code.description:
A picker works in a straight warehouse aisle. The storage slots are at integer metre positions given in visiting order; the picker starts at the first listed position, walks to every position in order, and finally walks back to the first position. Read N and then N positions into an array, then print the round trip report: the total walking distance (sum of absolute differences between consecutive positions plus the distance back to the first position), the farthest position, the average position with two decimals, and how many positions are strictly above that average.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N positions.

Output Format:
Total distance: <total metres walked>
Farthest position: <maximum position>
Average position: <average with 2 decimals>
Above average: <count of positions strictly greater than the average>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= position <= 10000
code.sampleoutput1:
Total distance: 20
Farthest position: 10
Average position: 6.00
Above average: 2
code.sampleoutput2:
Total distance: 0
Farthest position: 42
Average position: 42.00
Above average: 0
code.output1:
Total distance: 24
Farthest position: 9
Average position: 3.00
Above average: 1
code.output2:
Total distance: 0
Farthest position: 5
Average position: 5.00
Above average: 0
code.output3:
Total distance: 10000
Farthest position: 6000
Average position: 3500.00
Above average: 3

code.title: Stock Price Trade Analyzer
code.description:
A trading app studies the closing price of a stock over N days numbered from 0. One trade is allowed: buy on some day and sell on a strictly later day. Read N and then N prices into an array, then report the best trade: the earliest buy day and the earliest sell day that achieve the maximum possible profit (price difference between the sell day and the buy day). If no strictly later day gives a higher price, print No profitable trade.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N prices.

Output Format:
Buy day: <buy day index>
Sell day: <sell day index>
Profit: <price difference>
or the single line
No profitable trade

Constraints:
2 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= price <= 10000

code.title: Heatwave Streak Report
code.description:
A meteorological office tracks the maximum temperature for N days and flags a heatwave day when the temperature is strictly above a threshold. Read N, then N temperatures into an array, then the threshold. Find the longest run of consecutive heatwave days and report its length and its start day (the first reading is day 1). If several runs tie for the longest, report the earliest one.

Input Format:
One line with N + 2 integers: N, the N temperatures, then the threshold.

Output Format:
Longest streak: <length> day(s)
Start day: <1-based start day of the longest streak>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -50 <= temperature <= 60, at least one temperature is strictly above the threshold
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= N <= 1000, -50 <= temperature <= 60, at least one temperature is strictly above the threshold

code.title: Library Shelf Rearranger
code.description:
A librarian reorganises a shelf so that all even shelf codes come first and all odd shelf codes go to the back, while the relative order of the even codes among themselves and of the odd codes among themselves is preserved (a stable manual partition, no STL). Read N and then N shelf codes into an array, perform the rearrangement, then print the final arrangement and both counts.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N shelf codes.

Output Format:
The rearranged codes separated by single spaces on one line, then:
Even codes: <count of even codes>
Odd codes: <count of odd codes>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= shelf code <= 9999
